items.title: William Russell Interview, 1975-02-02
items.q: It's loud as Keppard or Wooden Joe or people like that.

ctx.x: So anyway, to get back to the point, Gene Williams had heard these records and agreed with me too that at least Bunk showed some possibilities. You couldn't really tell much how he played, both because his lip wasn't in shape and just by himself. The type of trumpet playing that Bunk did, which was a remarkable thing, and yet by itself it wouldn't sound that effective. Bunk was hardly ever on the beat, so if you didn't hear him patting his foot and all there, you could really tell of course where the beat is, but…
Well, of course, we'll never know what Joe Oliver really sounded like.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I've seen him play, and heard him play a whole parade when he'd be the only trumpet.

ctx.x: There wasn't any soloing as such then. Was there a soloing of instruments? It was all purely on sound.

There was, when Bunk was feeling good, he wouldn't ever put his horn down. In fact, that was the tradition in New Orleans. There might be sometimes, say, at times maybe the clarinet could have been a leader of a band, and he might have sort of featured himself at times. But ordinarily, the trumpet should never put his horn down at all. And that should go for a brass band, too, out on the street. Some of the guys in the old days would, like Wooden Joe, I know. I've seen him play, and heard him play a whole parade…
Is that how the solo got started? Well, I don't know.
